title: Eleven Hundred Metres Barefoot
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：winner　|　正文 317 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 winner 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: The ① winner in 1961 was a man nobody had heard of — forty-one years old, eleven seconds ahead, and never raced again, and a winner, he said, is only a person who was there. The ② winner of the cup, as the paper called him, was the same man, and they spelled his name wrong, and he kept the cutting for thirty-one years and pointed at it whenever anybody came in.

In 1968 the ③ winner was scored in the last minute by a boy of seventeen, and he never scored another, and my father said that is the whole of sport and the whole of most other things. The ④ winner of the 1974 final, which nobody now remembers, was a team from eleven miles away.

In 1979 there was one ⑤ winner in that village and eleven who were not, and the winner was not the shop with the better bread, and my grandmother said that is not a thing anybody can be taught. In 1981 the pie they put on at the fête was a ⑥ winner, by which she meant everybody wanted it, and they made eleven of them in 1982 and eleven in 1983 and then stopped, and nobody ever said why.

In 1989 the school asked a ⑦ prize winner back to speak to the children, and it was the girl from the next street, grown up, and she said there are no ⑧ winners in a village like that, only people who left and people who did not.

The ⑨ winner I remember, and I was eleven, crossed the line with his shoes in his hand, because the road had taken them, and he had run the last eleven hundred metres barefoot. The ⑩ winner my grandmother would have chosen, and she said so, was the man who came last and finished, in 1974, in the rain, at sixty-one, and the winner, she said, is not always the first.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: C. n. 赢家；占上风的一方
D. n. 极受欢迎／极为成功的东西（口语 a winner）
E. n. 制胜的一球；决定胜负的一击
F. 固定搭配：the winner of ... ……的获胜者
G. 固定搭配：a prize winner 获奖者；得奖者
H. 固定搭配：there are no winners in ... 在……中没有赢家

items.q: The winner in 1961 was a man
The winner of the cup, as the paper
the winner was scored in the last minute
there was one winner in that village
the pie they put on at the fête was a winner
the school asked a prize winner back
there are no winners in a village
The winner I remember, and I was eleven
The winner my grandmother would have chosen

answers.why: the winner 意为“获胜者、冠军”，1961 年的冠军是一个没人听说过的男人，四十一岁，领先十一秒。
the winner of the cup 意为“奖杯的得主”，报纸称他为奖杯得主，还把他的名字拼错了。
the winner 意为“制胜的一球、决定胜负的一击”，1968 年决定胜负的那一球是最后一分钟由一个十七岁的孩子打进的。
the winner of the 1974 final 意为“1974 年决赛的获胜者”，如今没人记得了，是十一英里外的一支队伍。
the winner 意为“赢家、占上风的一方”，1979 年村里只有一个赢家和十一个不是赢家的人，而赢家并不是面包做得更好的那家店。
a winner 意为“极受欢迎的东西、极为成功的东西”，1981 年他们在游园会上做的那个馅饼大受欢迎。
a prize winner 意为“获奖者、得奖者”，1989 年学校请回一位获奖者给孩子们讲话。
there are no winners in ... 意为“在……中没有赢家”，她说在这样一个村子里没有赢家，只有离开的人和留下的人。
the winner 意为“获胜者”，我记得的那个获胜者是手里拎着鞋冲过终线的，他光脚跑了最后的一千一百米。
the winner 意为“获胜者”，祖母会选的那个获胜者是 1974 年在雨中跑完的最后一名，六十一岁。

The winner of the cup, as the paper called him, had his name spelled wrong.
In 1968 the winner was scored in the last minute by a boy of seventeen.
In 1979 there was one winner in that village, and the winner was not the shop with the better bread.
In 1981 the pie they put on at the fête was a winner: they made eleven in 1982 and eleven in 1983.
In 1989 the school asked a prize winner back to speak to the children, and it was the girl from the next street.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 winner 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: The winner in 1961 was a man nobody had heard of, and the winner of the cup, as the paper called him, had his name spelled wrong.
In 1968 the winner was scored in the last minute by a boy of seventeen, and the winner of the 1974 final is nobody now remembers.
In 1979 there was one winner in that village and eleven who were not, and the pie they put on at the fête in 1981 was a winner.
In 1989 the school asked a prize winner back to speak, and she said there are no winners in a village like that.
The winner I remember crossed the line with his shoes in his hand, having run the last eleven hundred metres barefoot.
The winner my grandmother would have chosen was the man who came last and finished, in 1974, in the rain, at sixty-one.
